content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fails the fallback on affiliate coverage).**

- **Responsive grant:** § 1.4 (p0008–p0009) — HDI provides "the Company" with access to, and the right to use, the hosting system plus HDI's software and Content administration tools. This is the licence-type grant running in our favour.
- **Not walk-away:** no revocation-at-will or suspension right; the only exit is the mutual 90-day termination in § 4.1.
- **Fallback element already met:** § 10.3 (p0063) makes the Agreement inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by the parties' successors and assigns — successor transfer is covered, so no edit was made there.
- **Gap:** the grant names only "the Company", with no mechanism to add affiliates.
- **Cure:** one short sentence inserted after p0009 extending the § 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates on written notice to HDI (lowercase "affiliates" used deliberately, as the document defines no "Affiliate" term). Preferred features (contractors, perpetual/irrevocable paid-up licence) were not pursued given the hosting-services nature of the grant, and the narrow reciprocal Marks licence we grant HDI in § 6.1 benefits us and was left untouched.
